title: Burundi agricultural country profile evidence
purpose: Country 26 in the 54-country evidence programme. Record official agricultural census sources, crop-production observations, dated market-price leads and unresolved farm-budget inputs. This is not an activated calculator profile.

sources.title: RGPHAE 2024 Agricultural Module Reports
sources.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique du Burundi (INSBU)
sources.reference_period: 2024 general population, housing, agriculture and livestock census
available_material: Volume III: Statistical Tables of the Basic Agricultural Module
Volume IV: Analysis of the Basic Agricultural Module
Volume I and II: Community module statistical tables and analysis
2025 volumes covering modern agro-pastoral holdings and producer organisations
sources.note: INSBU identifies this collection as the official statistical reference for Burundi's agricultural sector. The public page is JavaScript-rendered; obtain the linked PDF volumes and extract crop-specific harvested/planted area, production, yield definitions, regions, farm structure, input use and livestock observations directly from the tables before accepting values.

sources.title: GIEWS Country Brief: The Republic of Burundi
sources.publisher: FAO Global Information and Early Warning System

observations.status: FAO estimate; cereal table reports 2019-2023 average 274 thousand tonnes, 2023 280 thousand tonnes and 2024 forecast 280 thousand tonnes. Forecast is not a final census observation.
FAO estimate; cereal table reports 2019-2023 average 146 thousand tonnes, 2023 125 thousand tonnes and 2024 forecast 136 thousand tonnes. Paddy basis; not milled rice.
FAO estimate; cereal table reports 2019-2023 average 22 thousand tonnes, 2023 25 thousand tonnes and 2024 forecast 25 thousand tonnes.
FAO forecast; aggregate only, not a crop-specific yield or calculator input.

quality_notes: The report gives production estimates but not matching crop-specific harvested area in the cited table; do not calculate or infer yield from these production values.
Burundi has three crop seasons: A, B and C; season C is concentrated in marshlands and irrigated areas. Preserve season and production-system distinctions.
FAO notes localized flood losses and below-average bean production in 2024, so a single national crop average may conceal substantial seasonal and regional variation.

sources.title: PNISAN Food Prices
sources.publisher: Burundi National Food and Nutrition Security Information Platform; price observations attributed to World Food Programme
sources.reference_period: Monthly market observations; latest published month shown as July 2026

observations.status: National median retail price; middle-half market range 1300-1700 BIF/kg, full observed market range 1000-2500 BIF/kg. July value is marked provisional.
National median retail price; not a farm-gate producer price.
Processed product retail price; not fresh cassava root farm-gate value.

quality_notes: PNISAN/WFP publishes monthly retail prices and validated observations; these must not be substituted for farm-gate output prices.
Separate maize grain from maize flour, yellow beans from other bean grades, and cassava flour from fresh cassava roots.
The platform provides downloadable price data; extract district/market-level observations and dates before using market-level estimates.

sources.title: Burundi Key Message Update: September 2026-January 2027

observations.status: FEWS NET reports most staple prices were relatively stable from August 2025 to August 2026, but 10-50 percent above five-year averages; bean prices increased around 10 percent year-on-year.
Fertilizer shortages, reduced seed stocks, higher labour and transport costs, foreign-currency constraints and fuel shortages are reported as factors affecting production and market access.
Below-average production risk is reported for the upcoming Season A due to delayed rainfall onset, fertilizer shortages and reduced planting intentions.

quality_notes: FEWS NET is a food-security analysis source, not a national farm-budget survey.
Use these findings as contextual risk flags and seek dated local input quotations and official crop survey data.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Burundi country brief archive
sources.note: The November 2024 brief documents three production seasons and regional variation in maize retail prices. Use it for historical context only, not as a current price series.

remaining_gaps: Download and extract INSBU RGPHAE 2024 Volume III basic agricultural statistical tables and Volume IV analysis; capture crop-specific area, production, yield definitions and province/commune breakdowns.
Extract the 2025 modern agro-pastoral holdings census tables for enterprise-level production and cost evidence where available.
Obtain matching harvested area and crop-specific yield observations for maize, paddy rice, beans, cassava and priority horticultural crops; keep Seasons A, B and C separate.
Extract dated producer/farm-gate prices by province, market, grade, product form and unit; keep these separate from PNISAN/WFP retail prices.

Obtain current farmer-paid prices for improved seed, fertilizer, crop protection, labour, mechanization, irrigation, land preparation and transport, including subsidy eligibility and actual farmer contribution.
Obtain livestock and poultry purchase prices, feed costs, veterinary costs, mortality, cycle length and output prices from official census tables and local supplier records.
Check currency denomination and any redenomination or exchange-rate reporting conventions in source tables before data entry.
extraction_status: Burundi's official INSBU 2024 agricultural census modules are identified as the primary national source, but table-level crop extraction is still pending. FAO's November 2024 brief provides crop-specific production forecasts (maize 280 thousand tonnes, paddy rice 136 thousand tonnes and sorghum 25 thousand tonnes) but not matching harvested area, so no yields are calculated. PNISAN/WFP provides dated July 2026 retail medians for white maize, yellow beans and cassava flour; these are explicitly not farm-gate prices. FEWS NET's September 2026-January 2027 update flags fertilizer shortages and elevated input/transport costs. No calculator values are admitted.
publication_decision: Do not activate Burundi in the farm-profit calculator until official crop area/yield tables, regional structure, dated farm-gate prices and farmer-paid input/labour costs have been extracted and reviewed.
next_steps: Download INSBU RGPHAE 2024 Volume III and IV and extract the crop tables with source page numbers and definitions.
Obtain district/province-level farm-gate prices and current input quotations; do not use retail prices as producer prices.
Build season-specific evidence for A, B and C before considering low/expected/high calculator values.
Keep the evidence research-only; do not modify calculator formulas or existing ten active country profiles.
